To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

14 suppressor mutations in the metY- nusA-infB-operon that suppress a ΔrimM growth defect increase the expression of rbfA by increasing the expression from thenusA gene and that the nusA gene is essential at 37 °C, as well as at 42°C.

the slow growth and reduced translational efficiency of a Δrim M mutant are suppressed by increased expression of the ribosome-binding factor RbfA and that nine of the suppressor mutations are in the nusA gene, increasing the read-through from the two transcriptional terminators just downstream of the metY gene.

the nusA gene is essential in Escherichiacoli at 37°C and that the nusAMutations suppress the growth defect of a ΔrimMutant by increasing the readthrough of two transcriptional terminators in the metYnusA-infBoperator.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of the expression of the metY, nusA, infB, and rbfA genes, which is important for the growth rate of E. coli.
the regulation of the metYNusA-infB-rbfA operon.
a new role for NusA in the control of ribosome synthesis and in the regulation of the expression of a gene encoding a protein involved in ribosome biogenesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the RimM protein is essential for the growth of E. coli at 37°C and above 31°C.

the nusA98 and nusA11 suppressors of the ΔrimM mutation increase expression of therbfA gene by decreasing termination of transcription at the internal terminators of the metYnusA-infB transcript and that this is the mechanism by which the ΔrimM mutant is suppressed.

the NusA protein is essential for growth of E. coli at 37°C, and the temperature sensitivity of the nusAMutations is a consequence of their inability to suppress the temperature-sensitive phenotype of the ΔrimM mutant at 42°C.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nusA gene is essential for the growth at 32, 37, and 42°C and that the growth rate of the ΔrimM mutant is dependent on the level of expression of the rbfA gene.
the nusA gene is essential at 37°, 42°, and 30°C and that it is required to maintain the integrity of the ribosome assembly process.
a deletion of therimM gene decreases the translational efficiency of a ΔrimA strain, and this defect is compensated by increased synthesis of RbfA, which is a component of the 30S subunit.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ribosome-binding factor RbfA is a major target for the feedback regulation of ribosome synthesis in E. coli.
the slow growth of a Δrimmutant can be suppressed by increased expression of the rbfA gene, which encodes a ribosome binding factor that is required to assemble the 30S ribosome.
the ribosomal proteins S1 and S2 are essential for the growth of E. coli at 37°C.
